statement.p: Determine the global extreme values of the function f(x,y)=x^{3}-2y, \quad 0 \le x,y \le 1

static.solution:
f_x(x,y)=3x^{2}=0, \quad f_y(x,y)=-2 The two equations have no solutions, hence there are no critical points.
The extreme values occur either at the critical points or at a point on the boundary of the domain.
To check the boundary we consider each edge of the square 0\le x,y \le 1 separately.
The segment \mathrm{OA}: On this segment y=0, 0\le x\le 1, and f takes the values f(x,0)=x^{3}.
The minimum value is f(0,0)=0 and the maximum value is f(1,0)=1.
The segment \mathrm{AB}: On this segment x=1, 0\le y\le 1, and f takes the values f(1,y)=1-2y.
The minimum value is f(1,1)=-1 and the maximum value is f(1,0)=1.
The segment \mathrm{BC}: On this segment y=1, 0\le x\le 1, and f takes the values f(x,1)=x^{3}-2.
The minimum value is f(0,1)=-2 and the maximum value is f(1,1)=-1.
The segment \mathrm{OC}: On this segment x=0, 0\le y\le 1, and f takes the values f(0,y)=-2y.
The minimum value is f(0,1)=-2 and the maximum value is f(0,0)=0.
The smallest value is f_{min}=-2 and it is the global minimum of f on the square.
The global maximum is the largest value f_{max}=1.
